text:
### Observed differences

- In the earlier window, A21, A22 and A23 were executed in every trace (200 of 200 each, exactly once per trace, around relative position 0.37 of the case); in the later window each appears in only about 1 in 200 traces. [OCC004, OCC005, OCC006, POS004, POS005, POS006]
- A14, A15 and A16 show the opposite pattern: they were not observed at all earlier, while in the later window each appears in about 30, 33 and 37 in 100 traces respectively (60, 65 and 74 of 200), around relative position 0.35 and at most once per trace. [OCC001, OCC002, OCC003, POS001, POS002, POS003]
- The three new activities behave as mutually exclusive alternatives: no later trace contains two of them, and together they appear in about 199 of 200 later traces. They also never share a trace with A21, A22 or A23. [REL001, REL002, REL010, REL003, REL011, REL018]
- Earlier, A21, A22 and A23 always ran together in the same trace without a fixed order among themselves (for example, A21 before A22 in about 52 in 100 traces and A22 before A21 in about 48); in the later window they no longer co-occur. [REL025, REL026, REL031]
- The neighbours of this segment are unchanged: earlier, A39 always preceded and A24 always followed the A21–A23 block; in the later window, every occurrence of A14, A15 or A16 is preceded by A39 and followed by A24. [REL027, REL028, REL032, REL033, REL036, REL037, REL006, REL007, REL014, REL015, REL021, REL022]
- The step distance from A39 to A24 shrank from 4 steps in all earlier traces to 2 steps in about 199 of 200 later traces, consistent with three activities between them being replaced by one. [LAG010]

### Inference

Support level: Supported hypothesis

The evidence supports the possibility that, in the later window, the mandatory segment between A39 and A24 changed from a block of three activities executed together — A21, A22 and A23, each once per trace in varying order — into a single activity drawn from three mutually exclusive alternatives, A14, A15 and A16 (about 30, 33 and 37 in 100 traces respectively), with A39 still before and A24 still after, two steps apart instead of four. This rests on direct, mutually consistent evidence across occurrence, relation, position and lag indicators: near-total participation flips (100% to about 0.5%, and 0% to 30–37 in 100), co-occurrence of the old trio dropping from every trace to none, mutual exclusivity of the new trio, and preserved flanking by A39 and A24. With 64 qualifying items against roughly 0.47 expected if nothing had changed, chance sampling cannot account for the evidence as a whole [OCC004, OCC001, REL025, REL001, REL027, REL006, LAG010, screening].

Other differences: A41 appeared in about 59 in 100 earlier traces and about 69 in 100 later traces; earlier it always co-occurred with A21 and typically ran after it, while later it co-occurs with one of A14/A15/A16 in most of its appearances, again usually after the new activity [REL030, REL009, REL017, REL024]. A24's mean relative position moved slightly earlier (about 0.43 to 0.39) and A39's slightly later (about 0.31 to 0.33), both remaining in all traces; A40 shifted marginally earlier [POS007, POS008, POS009].

Limitations: this describes a supported behavioural possibility, not a confirmed modification. Zero participation means only "not observed": A21–A23 could persist at a very low rate, since each still appeared in one later trace, and the evidence cannot fully rule out that the disappearance of the old block and the appearance of the new activities are two coincident changes rather than one replacement — though the preserved flanking and the shortened A39→A24 distance make a single replacement the more coherent reading. Detailed lag patterns inside the old block in the later window rest on a single trace and were not relied upon [OCC004, LAG001, LAG002, LAG003].
